card_summary: Vizrt, a company, partnered with students for a global broadcast. The broadcast utilized Vizrt technology, specifically for on-air operations, with potential implications for broadcast latency and bitrate management in live productions.
body_html:
At the On Air 2025 global broadcast event, students from around the world collaborated to produce a live, 24-hour program using Vizrt's graphics and video production tools. The event took place on a specific date and was streamed globally, showcasing the capabilities of the next generation of broadcast professionals. Vizrt's software was used to create real-time graphics, virtual sets, and video playout.

Technical Breakdown

Vizrt's graphics and video production tools utilize the ST 2110 standard for IP-based video and audio transport, allowing for flexible and scalable production workflows. The system also supports NMOS (Networked Media Open Specifications) for device discovery and registration, enabling seamless integration with other IP-based devices. Additionally, Vizrt's software uses the JPEG XS codec for low-latency, high-quality video compression, and the AES67 audio-over-IP standard for audio transport. The system's API allows for integration with other systems and devices, enabling automated workflows and real-time data exchange.

Operational Impact for Broadcast Engineers

The use of Vizrt's graphics and video production tools in the On Air 2025 event affects the playout and live production workflows, as engineers must evaluate and configure the system to meet the specific requirements of the event. This includes setting up the IP-based infrastructure, configuring device discovery and registration using NMOS, and ensuring low-latency video and audio transport using ST 2110 and AES67. Engineers must also consider the integration of the Vizrt system with other devices and systems, such as video switchers, audio mixers, and social media platforms.

Real-World Scenario

A regional TV station, such as a local affiliate of a major network, may consider using Vizrt's graphics and video production tools to enhance their live news and sports broadcasts. For example, they may use the system to create real-time graphics and virtual sets for their morning news program, or to produce interactive graphics and social media overlays for their live sports broadcasts. The station's engineers would need to evaluate the system's compatibility with their existing infrastructure, configure the IP-based transport and device discovery, and integrate the Vizrt system with their existing playout and production workflows.

Industry and Market Signals

The success of the On Air 2025 event using Vizrt's graphics and video production tools signals a shift in the market towards IP-based production workflows and the adoption of standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS. This trend is expected to continue, with more vendors developing products that support these standards and more broadcasters adopting IP-based workflows. The use of JPEG XS and AES67 also highlights the importance of low-latency, high-quality video and audio compression in live production environments. As the market continues to evolve, vendors will need to develop products that are compatible with these standards and can integrate with other IP-based devices and systems.

What to Watch Next

Engineers and technology directors should monitor the development of new products and standards that support IP-based production workflows, such as the upcoming releases of Vizrt's software and the development of new standards by the SMPTE and AMWA. They should also track the adoption of these standards and technologies by other broadcasters and vendors, and evaluate the compatibility of these products with their existing infrastructure. Additionally, they should watch for advancements in video and audio compression technologies, such as the development of new codecs and protocols, and the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into live production workflows.

Analysis: ST 2110 protocol enables flexible, IP-based signal routing for Vizrt's graphics and video playback systems, supporting low-latency broadcast workflows.
